analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: the Last-updated date (line 3) and a new paragraph at head lines 1960-1973. The paragraph documents that a JSON response_format (json_object or json_schema) on the Qwen template family defaults enable_thinking to false, so the template pre-closes the reasoning block. It says explicit user thinking controls override this default. It also says the coordinator prompt sidecar mirrors the rule so cache planning renders the same prompt. No executable code, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption paths change in the supplied evidence.

The only threat-model interaction I found is T-041 (prefix cache). Cache scope and identity depend on the rendered prompt. The doc says the coordinator sidecar renders the same prompt as the provider, and that public prompt vectors pin the Qwen-family JSON cases. The provider code and coordinator sidecar implementing this are not in the supplied batch. If the two renderers diverge, the result would be cache-planning misrouting or missed hits, not a cross-scope leak. The cacheSalt is coordinator-authored and folded into the SSD HMAC tag and chain hash. The doc does not alter account, model-build or prompt-contract scoping, TTL or at-rest crypto. The change also does not touch the TTL, disk budget, name derivation or DBK3 metadata that the T-041 detection_hint flags.

No regression, new attack surface or invalidated assumption is established by this documentation edit. The unverified contract is that the actual code (Qwen35TemplateFix and the coordinator sidecar) matches the described behavior. That belongs to review of the code-bearing parts of the PR, not this doc-only batch.
